title: Resonance of Fate
next_chapter_hook: In those hazy fragments of memory, a familiar figure heartbreakingly emerged—this was the truth Chen Ji least wanted to face in this life.

text.content:
At the moment the Void trembled, Chen Ji felt as if his chest had been struck by a ten-thousand-jin hammer.

The aura that pressed across the ages swept over him like a tide. He instinctively stepped back half a pace, fingers rapidly forming seals to activate the Tianji Record for divination—yet in the next instant, an even more violent tremor erupted from the depths of his bloodline.

Not Cang Yutian's pressure.

It was something older, more sorrowful, a resonance like two hearts beating simultaneously across infinite space and time, each pulse carrying the tremor of blood and tears.

Chen Ji covered his chest, his pupils contracting sharply.

The Tianji Record Fragment materialized from his embrace on its own, golden runes flickering madly—not as a warning, but as... guidance. It was directing him toward a certain direction—the extreme north, the Ancient Forbidden Land known as the 'Abyss of Heavenly Abandonment.'

The resonance grew increasingly intense, as if another heart was pressed against his chest, beating steadily and making his eyes ache with emotion.

That wasn't his own heartbeat.

No response.

Only that resonance seeped into his soul like silk threads, carrying an indescribable familiarity. Not the bond of blood kinship, yet deeper than blood; not the connection of a soul contract, yet more entwined than any pact.

Chen Ji suddenly felt a nameless fear.

In his life, he had orchestrated schemes across the world, leaving nothing to chance—yet he could never fathom his own heart. And now, this heart was responding to some distant existence, like scattered puzzle pieces finally finding each other.

At this moment, Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul quivered slightly from the first page.

The aged voice carried unprecedented solemnity: 'You sensed it.'

Not a question—a statement.

'Twin Fates... they are beings born from the same source as the Tianji Record. When the scales of fate失衡, they shall appear. And your connection with one of them runs deeper than I anticipated.'

Mo Xiansheng paused, and a trace of heartache even appeared in his voice: 'Child, once you step onto this path, there is no turning back.'

choice.prompt: That resonance was like a summons, piercing deep into the soul. Chen Ji felt a dull ache in his chest—that was another 'self' calling out. How should he choose?

choices.description: Following that pull, letting consciousness sink into the depths of resonance, perceiving everything about the other—even if it means enduring unknown pain.
choices.visible_reward: Glimpse partial truths of the Twin Fates
choices.risk_hint: Excessive resonance may damage the soul, and Heavenly Fate will significantly drain
choices.process_label: 承受撕裂之痛，窥探真相

text.content:
Chen Ji closed his eyes, allowing that resonance to devour him.

In an instant, the world spun. Countless images flashed by like a carousel—a figure with a similar outline to Chen Ji, bound by endless chains at the bottom of an abyss.

'It hurts... it hurts so much...'

That voice didn't emerge from his own mouth, yet it clearly echoed in his mind.

choices.description: Using the power of the Tianji Record to construct a barrier, steadying the mind, maintaining only minimal perception—calm observation, without rashly delving deeper.
choices.visible_cost: Unable to obtain more crucial information
choices.risk_hint: The resonance may be detected by the other party, leading to relationship rupture

text.content:
Chen Ji took a deep breath, his fingers rapidly sketching Tianji Record runes.

Golden light formed a thin barrier around him, isolating the surging resonance outside, leaving only a stream-like faint perception.

His spiritual sense was like a cold bystander, suspended above the abyss, watching the chained figure silently screaming.

The other party was in pain. Terrible pain.

choices.description: At all costs, sever this resonance—even if it means injuring oneself, taking fate firmly into one's own hands.
choices.visible_cost: May cause permanent trauma to the soul
choices.risk_hint: Forceful severance will cause violent backlash to Heavenly Fate, and may miss important truths

text.content:
Chen Ji's gaze turned sharp as ice, his palm pressing firmly against his chest.

"Dismantle!"

With a soft cry, the Tianji Record Fragment erupted with blinding white light, forcibly tearing apart that resonance line. Agonizing pain flooded through his entire body like a tide; he grunted, blood trickling from the corner of his mouth.

Meanwhile, deep within the Abandoned Abyss of the Extreme North, a figure bound by chains suddenly raised its head, eyes flashing with a trace of astonishment and... sorrow.

"Are you... going to abandon me too?"

The resonance—or rather, that broken connection—gradually grew clearer in Chen Ji's perception.

He saw a cage.

Not an ordinary prison, but shackles forged from the power of fate itself, pinning that figure死死钉在深渊最底层. Surrounding it were countless twisted runes, each one draining his strength, feeding on his suffering as nourishment.

That figure raised its head, meeting Chen Ji's gaze.

The same features, the same contours, even the same small mole at the corner of the eye. The only difference was—those eyes held no light left, only endless despair and unwillingness.

"You've finally come."

The voice was hoarse, as if it hadn't spoken for a thousand years, every word carrying blood.

Chen Ji felt his heart constrict sharply.

That wasn't pain.

It was the suffering of another "self,"穿越无尽虚空, directly seared onto his soul.

He watched the last flicker of light in those eyes extinguish, like a drowning person grabbing the final straw in darkness, only to find it was merely a cruel joke by fate.

"I've waited... for so long."

The voice carried a sob, yet forced a smile: "I thought... fate bringing us together must have its reason. Turns out... it was nothing but a deception."

Chen Ji clenched his fists, nails digging deep into his palms.

choice.prompt: The emotions transmitted through the resonance were so intense that the other figure's pain nearly overwhelmed Chen Ji. Emotion and reason clashed violently at this moment.

choices.description: Respond to that call with sincerity, trading heart for heart—even if it means letting one's own heart become riddled with holes.
choices.visible_cost: Heart's defense crumbles, possibly falling into the quagmire of the other's emotions
choices.risk_hint: Infected by the other's despair, oneself falls into danger

text.content:
Chen Ji slowly extended his hand,穿越虚空, touching that illusory figure.

At the moment their fingertips touched, endless emotions flooded into his heart like a deluge—loneliness, despair, unwillingness, the pain of being abandoned...

He couldn't help but speak, voice hoarse: "I'm sorry... I came late."

That figure froze, tears falling silently: "You... you're real..."

choices.description: Suppress the surging emotions in one's heart, calmly analyze the truth behind all this—why did fate bind them together?
choices.visible_cost: Appear cold and ruthless, possibly wounding the other's heart
choices.risk_hint: Reason may merely be self-deception; the truth could be even more brutal

text.content:
Chen Ji took a deep breath, forcing himself to calm down.

"Fate wouldn't let us meet without reason." He rapidly deduced in his heart, "The Tianji Record, the twin children of destiny, the Abandoned Abyss... there must be connections between these fragments."

Yet in the very moment of his contemplation, the light in that figure's eyes dimmed further.

"As expected... you're just like them, only wanting to use me."

Chen Ji's heart clenched painfully.

Just then, a strange and ancient will suddenly intervened.

"Interesting... the inheritor of the Tianji Record has actually formed a resonance with the exile."

The voice was cold and majestic, carrying a commanding scrutiny from above. Chen Ji instantly understood—this was the guardian of the Abandoned Abyss, or rather, the imprisoner.

"Fate has long written the script; you and I are merely pieces on a chessboard." That voice coldly laughed, "The fate of twin children was sealed from the moment of their birth—one inherits Heavenly Secrets, the other bears Heavenly Abandonment. What did you think you could change?"

Chen Ji felt the figure bound by chains tremble violently—that was fear deeply rooted in the marrow.

Had he... been told this before?

Chen Ji suddenly laughed.

That smile was cold and mocking, completely different from his usual weak good-for-nothing image.

"Pieces on a chessboard?"

He slowly spoke, voice not loud, yet every word clear: "In this life of mine, the thing I'm best at is overturning the chessboard."

The Tianji Record Fragment in his embrace trembled violently, golden runes spreading like living things, weaving complex and intricate strands of karma in the void.

That ancient will seemed stunned for a moment, then let out a mocking laugh: "With your pathetic fragment of the Tianji Record? Ridiculous..."

However, in the next instant, the laughter abruptly stopped.

Because Chen Ji saw it.

Within the strands of karma woven by the Tianji Record, the fates of that figure trapped in the abyss and his own—were indeed intertwined. But it wasn't fate...

It was human manipulation.

Someone, long ago, intentionally separated them, intentionally letting one bear Heavenly Secrets while the other bore Heavenly Abandonment. And the purpose of all this was actually to...

"Feed."

Mo Xiansheng's voice suddenly rang out, carrying unprecedented gravity: "This is the true purpose of the twin children of destiny—using one party's suffering to feed the other party's power. And you, Chen Ji, were supposed to be the one being fed."

choice.prompt: The truth exploded like thunder—Chen Ji was supposed to be the one being fed, yet accidentally became the inheritor of the Tianji Record. And that imprisoned "self" was the truly sacrificed existence. How should he choose?

choices.description: The other party is his twin child of destiny, the sacrificed other "self"—Chen Ji cannot sit by and watch, even if it means making enemies of all Heaven and Earth.
choices.visible_cost: Exposing one's own strength, possibly drawing the gaze of the Eye of Heavenly Dao
choices.visible_reward: Gain the recognition and trust of the twin child of destiny
choices.risk_hint: The road of opposing fate is fraught with difficulties and dangers

text.content:
Chen Ji closed his eyes, and when he opened them again, his gaze had turned ice-cold.

"I've noted it."

He looked at the figure trapped in the abyss, his voice low but firm: "Wait for me."

His consciousness began to withdraw from the resonance. The figure stared at him in astonishment, lips trembling: "You... you're really coming?"

"As I said—" Chen Ji curled his lips, "What Chen Ji does best is overturn the chessboard."

choices.description: Exposing strength at this moment would be tantamount to self-destruction. We must first gather more intelligence, scheme in the shadows, and wait for the opportune moment.
choices.visible_cost: The other party may endure more suffering during this period
choices.risk_hint: The longer time drags on, the more dangerous the other party becomes

text.content:
Chen Ji withdrew his hand, his expression returning to calm.

"I need time."

The voice transmitted through the resonance, carrying a composed promise: "Give me time, and I will find a way."

The figure fell silent for a long while, then finally nodded slightly: "Alright... I'll wait for you."

The resonance gradually faded, and the figure's outline began to blur. But before completely vanishing, Chen Ji heard one final sentence—

"My name is... Chen Nian."

Chen Nian.

The name struck like thunder in Chen Ji's mind.

No.

Impossible.

Chen Nian was his missing sister, the "Heavenly Fate Lock Key" taken by the Holy Sect, the person he had schemed across the world to find—how could she be a Destined Twin? How could she be the "self" imprisoned in the Abyss of Heavenly Abandonment?

Unless...

A terrible thought surfaced.

Chen Nian was never just his sister. Or rather, was the identity "Chen Nian" merely a mask fate had assigned her?

Mr. Mo's voice sounded at the opportune moment, carrying a sigh: "You're finally beginning to touch upon the truth."

"Chen Nian and the Destined Twin were born from the same source. Her existence interferes with the Tianji Record's foresight because her fate has never been within the Heavenly Secrets—she is the variable, the key to breaking destiny."

"This is precisely why the Eye of Heavenly Way is so eager to keep her under control."

Chen Ji felt a bone-deep chill.

In all his life, he had calculated every detail and advanced with careful strategy. Yet he had never imagined that his beloved sister had been the largest piece on destiny's chessboard from the very beginning.

And all his schemes—perhaps had been anticipated by others all along.

The moment the resonance completely severed, Chen Ji's eyes snapped open.

Cold sweat had soaked through his back. He discovered he was still standing in the same spot, with no change in the surrounding scene, as if everything just now had been nothing more than an illusion.

But he knew it was real.

The Tianji Record Fragment lay quietly in his embrace, its golden rune light considerably dimmer than before—the price of consuming vast amounts of Heavenly Fate.

And in his heart, there was a burden he had never carried before.

Chen Nian... Destined Twin... the sacrificed other "self"...

These fragments kept spinning in his mind, piecing together an increasingly clear outline.

Right then, a familiar cold harrumph came from behind.

"Chen Ji, you acted on your own again."

Su Qingyao had appeared nearby at some point, her beautiful eyes carrying scrutiny and... concern?

"Inner Disciple Senior Fellow." Chen Ji quickly concealed his expression, switching to that harmless waste-of-talent appearance, "I merely... sensed something."

Su Qingyao furrowed her brow, seeming about to speak, but ultimately just sighed: "The entire Tianqing Sect is on alert for the Ultimate Chess Player's arrival. If you want to die, don't implicate the sect."

Though harsh in words, her footsteps unconsciously drew closer.

Chen Ji noticed, the corner of his mouth lifting slightly.

This cold and formidable Inner Disciple Senior Fellow was becoming increasingly bad at hiding her thoughts.

Deep within the Abyss of Heavenly Abandonment in the Extreme North.

The figure bound by chains slowly raised his head, gazing at the eternal darkness above where no starlight could ever be seen.

"Chen Ji..."

He murmured to himself, and a smile actually appeared at the corner of his lips. It was the first time in a thousand years that he had smiled.

"So... even fate can play jokes."

He closed his eyes, feeling that trace of faint warmth in his chest—the remnant of resonance, and his sole reason for living.

"I will wait for you."

The voice was soft, yet carried an unwavering certainty.

"Just as you waited for Chen Nian."

And at this moment, in that higher, more profound void above, a pair of invisible eyes quietly observed all of this.

The Eye of Heavenly Way.

It held no anger, no agitation, not even the slightest emotional fluctuation. In its billion-year existence, it had witnessed too many insignificant creatures who believed they could defy heaven's will.

"Interesting."

That transcendent willslightly颤动，像是在品味一道新奇的点心。

"The Tianji Record's inheritor has formed a resonance with the exiled one... The script of destiny seems to have encountered some interesting variables."

"But variables... are themselves part of the script."

The Eye of Heavenly Way slowly closed, falling into a long slumber.

The chess game has only just begun.
